thread:
jay: Heads-up: getting multiple p99 latency alerts for /v1/generate on hosted region-us-west-2 starting ~12:05 UTC. p95 up 30%, p99 up ~2-3x. No error rate increase. Anyone else seeing this?
anya: I saw the alerts, digging in graphs now. Config didn't change on the API side. Looks correlated with the runtime deploy from earlier today (PR #2789 — kernel selection heuristics).
pranav: Confirming — that release switched preference to FlashAttention by default for 4096 context models on A100. We thought it was safe after perf tests.
derek: Can you paste the perf numbers? I have a repro harness I can run against canary.
jay: Here are quick numbers from alerting dashboard: baseline p95 ~120ms, p95 now ~160ms, p99 baseline ~320ms, p99 now ~900ms. Spike started at 12:04:33 UTC.
anya: Stack traces from traces-api indicate more frequent CUDA synchronizations around attention kernel calls. Looks like some kernels are falling back to a slower path under certain sequence lengths.
pranav: Hmm, one hypothesis: FlashAttention kernel path in Triton sometimes uses SDPA fallback on odd batch-size boundaries which blows up for small batches. Could be an index misalignment with kv-cache and dynamic batching.
maria: Repro steps I ran locally (A100) that reproduce p99: run this.

```
# repro script
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-large-8k","input":"token-stream","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```

maria: With 200 concurrent requests p99 jumps similar to prod. Lowering concurrency to 50 removes spike.
pranav: Ok that matches a batching boundary issue. To validate quickly, try toggling the FlashAttention flag on the runtime instance.
derek: How? Is there a runtime flag?
pranav: Yes — on the runtime hosts set env REDWOOD_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 and restart the inference-worker process. Also there's a per-model override in model-config: "kernel_preference": "sdpa".
anya: I pushed a quick feature-flag to rollback kernel heuristic: ff:kernel-select -> off for region-us-west-2 canary group (5%). Rolling now.
ops-bot: @channel Feature flag kernel-select toggled: region-us-west-2 canary group (5%) disabled. Time: 12:27 UTC.
jay: Any quick logs we should collect to confirm?
pranav: Capture per-request kernel selection logs (set LOG_KERNEL=debug) and GPU metrics (nvprof / nsys or perf metrics exported to prometheus). Also collect sample traces for p99 requests.
derek: I ran the repro with REDWOOD_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 locally — p99 back down to ~340ms (still slightly above baseline but far better than 900ms). That confirms FlashAttention is implicated.
maria: I filed a bug: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/IM-4127 with sample traces and nsys output. Adding PR #2791 which pins kernel to sdpa for rw-large-8k while we investigate.
support-bot: Notifying affected customers in tickets: CS-1123, CS-1155. Suggested temporary mitigation: use model-config override or request Dedicated routing.
pranav: Short-term mitigation plan:
- keep kernel-select ff disabled on region-us-west-2 for Canary then ramp down to 0% (complete rollback) if metrics look good
- pin impacted models to sdpa via model-config
- publish rollback notes in release channel
- open root cause investigation: look into Triton/Triton-Pytorch fusion and the FlashAttention -> SDPA fallback condition
anya: Doing the rollback ramp now to 0% (full rollback) — ETA 12:42 UTC.
ops-bot: Rollout update: kernel-select flag rolled back to 0% in region-us-west-2. Time: 12:41 UTC.
jay: Post-rollback numbers from prod: p95 ~125ms, p99 ~340ms. Much improved but still above historical p99 320ms.
pranav: There might be residual cache effects; also PR introduced a compile flag change (NVCC_FLAGS="--expt-relaxed-constexpr -O3 -DNDEBUG -use_fast_math") that could change FP behavior. I'll diff the build artifacts and kernel binaries.
derek: Could the quantization/graph-opt path interact? We also changed default nvFuser setting in runtime config to "enabled".
maria: I compared kernel SHAs: fused_attn_v2 (new) vs fused_attn_v1 (old) — v2 has a change in indexing to favour warp-level tiling. Under odd seq_len it's slower; reproducer attached in IM-4127 shows the branching.
pranav: Plan for medium-term:
- revert nvFuser toggle until kernel is validated across sequence lengths
- add unit/regression perf test that runs quad combinations: batch sizes 1-16, seq len 128/512/1024/2048/4096 on A100 to catch p95/p99 regressions
- add telemetry: kernel_id chosen per request + latency histogram bucketed by (batch, seq_len)
- consider adding SDPA fallback threshold and disable fallback to slow path
- collaborate with Triton/FlashAttention upstream on potential bug
anya: I already opened a PR to add the regression perf test and telemetry: PR #2793. Review welcome.
maria: For immediate customer messaging: recommend we tell affected customers we rolled back the kernel heuristic and applied per-model pin while we add tests. CS drafted a note, can review in #customer-success.
jay: Nice work everyone. Actions:
- pranav: diff build artifacts & revert nvFuser (short-term)
- anya: merge perf tests and telemetry (PR #2793)
- maria: update bug IM-4127 with traces and customer impact
- derek: help run expanded repro across instance types (A100, H100) and quantized variants
- support-bot: mark tickets CS-1123/CS-1155 resolved pending customer confirmation
Anything else? :eyes:
pranav: Also scheduling a 1hr postmortem if root cause persists after triage. Tentatively 16:00 UTC.
anya: Ping me if you need help with telemetry schema. I'll add kernel_id to the request span.
support-bot: CS tickets updated. Customers notified about rollback and temporary mitigation. :white_check_mark:
jay: Closing the thread for now — will reopen if anomalies reappear. Thanks all :pray:
